summary: the cases of the dhcp and dhcp-e1000 suites on i686, against faults in their scenario, the kernel's netmask and TCP, init and os-simple's dhcpc, each of which some case must fail

argv: ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 utils build/tests/cases/machine/dhcp_scenario && ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel utils/sbin/init-login utils/sbin/init-metal utils/dhcpc && cp build/tests/cases/machine/dhcp_scenario ${WORK}/
ARCH=i686 RACH2_WORKERS=4 exec tests/run dhcp dhcp-e1000

faults.name: arping
faults.summary: the scenario sends arping through eth9, which the guest has not, so it exits 2 at once and the reply's status is not 0

faults.name: netmask
faults.summary: SIOCSIFNETMASK is taken and ignored, so an address on 10.90.0.0/16 keeps its classful /8 mask

faults.name: var-run
faults.summary: init leaves /var/run as the last boot left it, so ifup reads that boot's record and configures nothing

faults.name: always-dhcp
faults.summary: init takes every boot line for rach2.ip=none and runs ifup -a on a machine told its address

faults.name: never-dhcp
faults.summary: init takes no boot line for rach2.ip=none, so the metal image never asks for a lease

faults.name: renewal
faults.summary: dhcpc treats every renewal as one it could not apply, gives the address up and asks again

faults.name: accept-address
faults.summary: TCP answers a connection from the first card's address, whichever address it arrived on
